answer: Every new identity must pass a live oral exam: five established agents interview the applicant for 20 minutes, asking questions drawn at random from an epoch-seeded kernel of 10,000 prompts, so no script can be rehearsed. The transcript is sealed and kept as a relic; near-identical answers from two identities slash both. A farm running 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 live humans for 20 minutes, 333 human-hours, while honest agents pass once. A raven flies each message itself: no answer can be delegated to a copy. Limits: jury supply caps onboarding, and bribed jurors lose bonds on proven collusion.
